expectation: Membrane/cytoplasmic ring on antigen-presenting cells (macrophages, DCs, B cells) and on activated T cells, sometimes on tumour cells. Common in the immune stroma: scattered or clustered dendritic-shaped cells in tumour stroma and aggregates, sparse inside tumour nests.
observed: A: strong, uneven HLADR in stromal, network-like cells; some cores are much brighter than others and a few are nearly empty. B/C: scattered membranous stromal cells, with tumour nests dark. D: a bright cell with membrane-shaped signal. E: HLADR outlines cells and partly overlaps CD14 (white), with HLADR+CD14− areas.
why: Bright membranous HLADR sits on a distinct stromal/immune subset that differs by core and overlaps part of the CD14 population, as an APC marker should.
notes: HLADR marks dendritic and macrophage-like stromal cells with membrane outlines and is absent from tumour nests. Part of the stain overlaps CD14 cells. Brightness differs a lot between cores, but the pattern follows cell types, not tissue density.
